Description:
Now, ye might've heard a tale or two about dwarves. Some true, most twisted by long-tongued humans who've never held a pickaxe in their lives. There's more to us than stone and ale... though I'll not deny we fancy both. There are the rune-carvers, aye, clever lot, some etch their runes for warding and protection, others for blasting holes in mountains... or enemies. Then there's the Irontouched, deep below the roots of the world, whose skin gleams like hammered steel and whose beards shimmer gold as morning sun on a mug of mead. I've seen one once... or so I claim when the ale's strong enough!
Now, don't go askin' about the womenfolk's beards, mind you. Some do, some don't, and that's all ye need to know.
Every dwarf's born with hands that itch to build. We carve homes into mountains, we forge ships stout enough to kiss the sea's fury, and we raise tombs so grand the dead feel right at home. Feh, we're probably sitting right on top of a lost dwarven underground civilization ready to have its treasure looted! But if ye ever find yerself near the northern shores… best pray the wind's on yer side. The raider clans there? Wild as thunder and twice as loud. They'll drink with ye one night and raid yer village the next, and still call ye “friend” when they're done!
Aye, we're stubborn folk, proud folk. The mountains and lands remember our names long after we've passed.
BookDescription:
Excavation Record

The tablet was discovered standing upright behind a collapsed wall. No chamber exists beyond the wall. No tool marks indicate how it was placed there. The strange runes on the ground around the tablet seem to indicate a mixed irontouched and stonekin society.

  If these words are read, then our halls have finally fallen silent.
  Do not mourn us.
  Stone remembers us well enough.

The phrase translated as "fallen silent" may also be read as "ceased to answer." Neither interpretation is universally accepted. The following three lines are badly weathered. Several runes appear to have been intentionally chiseled away.

  Many shall believe we dug too deep.
  Many shall blame the mountain. [possibly a different word]
  Those who remain behind shall not be remembered.
  Those who depart shall not speak of the journey.
  They shall...

The rest of the translation is redacted, and is to be reported directly to the society above. According to the historians, the doors of these chambers are older than the city surrounding them. Every dwarven ruin around contains rooms that appear never to have been entered, and several of their constructions feature rocks newer around the foundation and older at the top. For every sane person, that springs to mind one question: they built cities from the top-down? How is that possible?

The excavation has been suspended indefinitely following the discovery of a sealed chamber beneath the archive. The tablet will be taken to one of our temples of the Flame. It seems to match the inscriptions we uncovered several miles away. If my research is correct, I might have the Flame passed onto me.


Tablet II - On the Children of Iron
"...Those who descended into the Fifth Furnace of the north returned with skin that no blade could shame. Whether they became iron, or iron became them, none could say... When the long winter of ash came, they buried themselves beneath the white earth. Spring remembered them, though we had forgotten..."

The tablet clearly refers to the irontouched dwarves, and seems to depict the origin of their species - skin akin to metal, beards and hair thick and luscious as gold, and eyes hard and translucent as gems. The term "Fifth Furnace" appears nowhere else in surviving dwarven records. Some scholars argue it refers to the aftermatch of the cataclysm brought about by the ancient dwarves: valleys were said to become glass beneath a single sun forged by dwarven hands, dropped onto the ground, forming a tree of fire and smoke in the sky above. The modern blue-skinned Uldran communities living in the frozen extremities of Earthguard continue the practice hibernation. Whether this custom originated from necessity or ritual remains disputed. Their relation to the irontouched remains unknown. Though both closely resemble dwarves in traits and physionomy, several studies indicate vastly different biochemistry. The question remains: are they both dwarves?



Tablet XI - Those Who Walked the Forest

  "We warned them that roots make poor roofs. They answered that trees remember storms better than stone"

This is the earliest known reference to forest-dwelling dwarves. Later tablets imply they willingly abandoned mountain life, though no reason is given to live among the wood elves and worship mother nature and her many goddesses of storms, forests, and oceans (note: Ocea, their goddess of the ocean, is clearly a distinct concept from the longshore civilizations of dwarves who, instead, prefer worship through conquest by sea). Alas, the Flame forbids politheistic religions.

Tablet XXV - Those of Stone
  
  We celebrated, for they would never leave home.
  We mourned, for they would dig their own graves.

No contemporary account explains whether Stonekin are hereditary, blessed, cursed, or crafted. All four theories remain popular.

Language: You speak Common, Dwarvish and a number of chosen languages equal to your Focus or Presence (whichever is higher).

~Stouthearten~.Effect:
You have +100% Inventory capacity.
You can wear an extra layer of Light or Medium armor over (or underneath) your armor. Apply all of its effects as normal.
~Stouthearten~.Notes: Unarmored is not an armor. 50% Damage reductions of the same type do not stack
~Stouthearten~.Name: ~Stouthearten~

Starting Abilities Description.Stouthearten:
Dwarves are slow folk - they usually need a lot of rest to be able to do their tasks.
However, that does not mean they are lazy; quite the contrary. Dwarves are very sturdy, hence their unique ability to be able to wear two sets of armor, in which it would normally be very difficult to move around.

~Forgeborn~.Effect:
Spend 1 hour at a forge while in a friendly town to craft an artisanal Two-Handed weapon or an armor, that's made of metal.
Spend {Gold}Gold equal the item's base cost + 100.
If it's a Two-Handed weapon, it deals +1 Damage. If it's an armor, its wearer has +2 Max Health.
~Forgeborn~.Upgrade: For example, you can't craft padded armor, robes, leather armor, etc.
~Forgeborn~.Notes: Smelting, forging, and crafting - must-know skills for many dwarves. It is not just a mere rumor that many of the best blacksmiths are dwarves, or have been born and raised in Forgeborn dwarf societies.
~Forgeborn~.Name: ~Forgeborn~

~Uldran Ancestry~.Effect:
You can spend 12 hours sleeping to recover 1d8 Health or get -50% Cold Damage taken until the end of next Combat.

Also, you can choose to hibernate for 48 hours to cure all your minor diseases and poisons.
~Uldran Ancestry~.Upgrade: Loud noises and movement still wake you up as they normally would.
~Uldran Ancestry~.Notes: The nordic dwarves have made hibernation a core skill to surviving the harsh winters of the mountains.
~Uldran Ancestry~.Name: ~Uldran Ancestry~

~Shoreraider~.Effect: When defeating people, your team loots +10% {Gold}Gold and goods like gems, metals, textiles, etc.
~Shoreraider~.Notes: Long boats, wooden homes and raiding parties are the common sight you grew up with, and you have learned much about these crafts throughout the years, for better or worse...
~Shoreraider~.Name: ~Shoreraider~

~Stonekin~.Effect: Use when you or an ally takes Damage that would make them fallen. That Damage is reduced by 100%.
~Stonekin~.Notes: Certain subspecies of dwarves come from Stonekin clans, and are fit for roles of leadership due to their thick, almost stone-like textured skin and temper.
~Stonekin~.Name: ~Stonekin~

~Rúndottir~.Effect: Inscribe one of the Runes below onto a weapon as an _extra Rune_, without actually needing to have that Rune.
~Rúndottir~.Upgrade: The weapon will also have its regular Rune slot, aside from this _extra Rune_.
~Rúndottir~.Notes: Some dwarven communities rely on runes for protection, enchantment and utility. Many of their buildings are laid out on key coordinates representing numbers or conceprs with strong meanings, and their clothes are often woven in the shape of constelations for good fortune and increased control over magic.

SpellTable.Name: Elemental Rune
SpellTable.Effect: Choose Fire, Cold or Shock. The attacker can freely change the Damage Type of the weapon to that element.

SpellTable.Name: Spirit Rune
SpellTable.Effect: Change any one Stat written on it to ^Focus^, ^Presence^, or ^Presence^.

SpellTable.Name: Lodestone
SpellTable.Effect: +2 Damage if the weapon scales with no Stat

SpellTable.Name: Wind Rune
SpellTable.Effect: Remove all Stat requirements for the weapon.

~Rúndottir~.Name: ~Rúndottir~

~Irontouched~.Effect: You have -1 Instinct, but +5 Max Health.
~Irontouched~.Notes:
Your skin has a metal-like sheen to it, your beard and hair are thick like metal strings and your finger nails resemble gems the same color as your eyes. As you age, these become more and more valuable, even being made of gold and emeralds in your days of age.
Dwarves with Irontouched ancestries have learend to be wary of strangers and bandits, many of whom will not waste the chance to kill and sell Irontouched body parts for money.
~Irontouched~.Name: ~Irontouched~

~Landliving~.Effect: You know have a Level 1 Druid Talent. You can change it inbetween Adventures.
~Landliving~.Notes: From more obscure and hidden dwellings around the world, the Landliving dwarves inhabit forests, hill-houses and sometimes swamps, and have learned to live off the land. However, some of them are said to innately wield nature magic, and they may be regarded as oddly special or particularly uncanny.
~Landliving~.Name: ~Landliving~
